official_skills.notes: Generates unit tests. It does not decide which layer a given behavior belongs in - that judgment stays with the mentor.
Vendor skill, not a framework-team skill. It uses a different CLI (agentskillsforall) than the skills CLI. Recommend it as an option, not as the default.

gap_map.why_it_matters: No Flutter framework-team skill decides which behavior belongs in a unit, widget, golden or integration test. Teams default to whatever is easiest to write, which is usually the slowest layer.
Layout and routing skills operate inside a widget. Nothing tells the agent when a feature folder has outgrown itself or when a widget should become a package.
gap_map.fallback: The mentor applies references/growth-signals.md with the stack thresholds below.

gap_map.why_it_matters: Golden tests fail across platforms because of font and pixel rendering differences. A test suite that only passes on one machine erodes trust in the whole suite.
gap_map.fallback: The mentor requires goldens to run on a pinned CI image and treats local golden failures as environment noise until proven otherwise.

testing.notes: Golden tests are visual regression, not behavior. They need a pinned CI environment to avoid cross-platform pixel differences. Never regenerate goldens to make a failure disappear without looking at the diff.

growth_thresholds.extract_component_library: >=3 occurrences of the same widget across >=2 feature folders
growth_thresholds.extract_package: >=2 features import the same internal module
growth_thresholds.split_widget: a build() method exceeds 100 lines, because the widget is doing layout and logic at once

layers.name: UI - View
layers.must_not: hold business logic; only conditional rendering, animation, layout and simple routing

layers.name: UI - ViewModel
layers.holds: most of the application logic: transforms repository data, holds UI state, exposes commands
layers.must_not: know about widgets it does not own - one view maps to exactly one view model

layers.name: Data - Repository
layers.holds: the source of truth for model data: caching, retries, error handling, transforming raw data into domain models

layers.name: Data - Service
layers.holds: wrappers over external sources - REST endpoints, platform APIs, local files - returning Future or Stream

layers.name: Domain - Use case
layers.holds: logic that merges several repositories or is duplicated across view models
layers.must_not: exist before a second view model needs it

variants.name: Two layers (UI + Data), no domain layer
variants.use_when: the default. View models talk to repositories directly.
variants.cost: logic shared by several view models gets duplicated before you notice it

variants.name: Three layers (UI + Domain + Data)
variants.use_when: a second view model needs the same composed logic, or one view model has to merge several repositories
variants.cost: one more hop for every read; premature use-cases are the over-abstraction signal in growth-signals.md

rules: A view holds no business logic. Conditional rendering, animation, layout and simple routing only.
One view maps to exactly one view model. A view model serving two views is a signal the feature is really two.
A repository never imports another repository. Composition across repositories belongs in a use case.
A service returns raw data. Business rules live above it.
Do not add the domain layer until a second view model needs the same logic.
architecture.component_library: Extract to a shared component library at >=3 occurrences of the same widget across >=2 features - matching growth_thresholds.extract_component_library. Atomic Design is a way to organise that library once it exists; it is not a reason to create one.
architecture.notes: The Flutter team defines a feature as one paired view + view model, which is why the folder strategy is feature-first rather than layer-first.

dead_code_risks: Generated code (*.g.dart, *.freezed.dart, *.mocks.dart) - never edit or delete by hand, regenerate with build_runner
Widgets referenced only by golden tests
Route names referenced as strings in a router table
Classes registered by name in a service locator (get_it and similar)
Platform channel handlers referenced only from Kotlin/Swift sources
